explanation: Passing excess carbon dioxide through a suspension of calcium carbonate dissolves it into soluble calcium bicarbonate — the reverse of the reaction that makes limewater turn milky, and the reaction behind how CO2-rich water erodes limestone caves.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: A milky white calcium carbonate suspension in water, with excess carbon dioxide bubbled in.
beaker_view.final_appearance: A clear, colourless solution once the cloudiness has dissolved.
beaker_view.observation: As more carbon dioxide is bubbled through, the milky cloudiness gradually clears as it dissolves into soluble calcium bicarbonate.
